description.purpose: One generation of one person's agent, as a level. A level owns what its siblings must share, and what the parts of one generation share is exactly three things: the CONVERSATION SURFACE that keeps its sessions and calls its brain (surface -- a sealed talky), the REASONING CORE it consults (cogny -- a second opinion that answers as its own turn) and the TOOL SURFACE it calls (tools -- one node, one contract, `tool_call` in and `tool_result` out). Three refs and no container: since 2.0.0 the CHANNELS are gone from this level (GH #454). A channel belongs to the person, not to one of their generations, so it stands in `<member>/channels` and reaches this assistant by addressing its path. What that buys is the whole point of the move: one bot can serve two agents of the same person, a screen has an owner, and a generation swap does not take the chat account with it. Since 2.1.0 ([#458](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/458)) the level carries `in_pack` / `pack_ack`: a durable `system.*` slot -- an identity, a persona, a handover, and since [#488](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/488) the agent's own `instructions` -- reaching the generation from outside, fanned out to the surface AND the core because one generation is one person's agent and its brains must not disagree about who that is. Adding a lane in each direction is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). The occupants moved once more inside the same unreleased wave, and the level moved with them without a new number: `talky@4.6.1` / `cogny@4.6.1` ask the tool surface for the declarations of the tools they use ([#464](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/464)), so this level draws the four edges that pair needs -- `schemas` out to `./tools` and `in_menu` back, once for the surface and once for the core, told apart by `context.tool_caller` exactly as a tool result is. Both halves are consumed INSIDE the level, so no lane crosses this boundary: nothing a caller out here can do is new, and a version is a shipped fact -- `2.1.0` has not shipped, so it is extended rather than superseded. Since GH #475, still inside that same unreleased wave, the level also passes the TRANSFER lanes of its surface's session keeper through -- `in_export` and `in_import` in, `dump` out, three plain edges and no modifier -- because the sessions of a generation were the last thing a member could export a copy of itself without: the keeper answers the lane, nothing above it forwarded one, and a colony rebuilt from its own export greeted a person it had been talking to for a year as a stranger. Since [#516](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/516) the level also decides WHICH MODEL each of its two brains infers with, and it is the only place that can: `talky` and `cogny` both read the ctx key `model` in their brain, both are right to standalone, and a level that references both is instantiated with ONE flat ctx -- so both resolved the same key and the conversation surface ran the reasoning model, every turn paying core latency for the half whose whole job is to answer fast. The fix is one line on the ref marker (`./talky` names `model_surface` for the cell it references, through the `override_params` a ref has carried since GH #277) plus the `requires` block below, which is this level's first: the key is STRICT, because a defaulted surface model would re-open the same silence one layer down. `model` and `model_fast` are NOT restated there -- they are inherited through the ref chain (GH #292), and restating them is the drift that declaration exists to remove. Neither occupant moved. The number did not move either: `2.1.0` has not shipped, so it is extended rather than superseded, exactly as it was for #464 and #475 inside this same unreleased wave. Since 2.2.0 ([#529](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/529), [#530](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/530)) the level draws the SECOND `schemas` / `in_menu` pair -- surface to CORE and back -- and retires the second errand name. Both follow from one thing only this level can know: `consult_cogny` is not a tool of any hive, it is the errand this level routes from `./talky` to `./cogny`, so the side that ANSWERS it is the side that can declare it. Its schema used to be a hand-typed seed row in the surface's brain; #464 replaced the hand-typed menu with an asked-for one and the row went with it, leaving a charter that named a tool the menu no longer carried. So the surface now asks BOTH occupants what they serve, each answers what it has, and the collector merges the two halves by `context.tool_answerer` -- the mirror of the `tool_caller` the request already carried. The declared list is this level's too, on the same ref marker that names the surface's model and for the same reason. `ask_memory` is gone in the same act: the lookup class assumed the core could answer a memory question and the core has no memory leg, while the surface has one one hop away through its own `memory_recall`. One edge removed, two added; the level's edge count lives in its README, once, where a drift lock derives it from this file. No lane crosses this boundary either way, so nothing a caller out here can do is new -- the second digit, and the removal is the removal of an internal edge condition, never of an address. Still inside 2.2.0, [#535](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/535) sets the THIRD override on that same ref marker and moves no edge: `collector/assemble.memory_tier` is "1" for the surface, so the conversation half reads the member's memory BEFORE it calls its brain instead of only when its model decides to ask. `collector` ships the knob empty and `talky` leaves it that way, correctly -- standalone there is no hive beside it and a per-turn `recall` would leave for an address nobody wired -- and this level is the only place that knows it was instantiated into a member that HAS one. The tool stays: `memory_recall` is the deliberate lookup, the ambient leg is what the fast half reads before it answers at all, and the reasoning core keeps its own `memory_tier` empty because a problem solver asks about a time range on purpose (#528). One param key, no lane and no address, so the number is extended rather than superseded, exactly as for #464, #475 and #516 inside this same unreleased wave. Since 2.3.0 ([#545](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/545)) the conversation surface is called `talky`, after the template it references, where it was called `surface` after the role it plays: a ref onto template X is a directory called X, and 19 of the library's 22 ref markers -- `./cogny` and `./tools` on this level among them -- were already spelled that way. 26 of the 37 edges carry the name, and the two stamped tokens are renamed with it (`context.recall_caller` and `context.tool_caller` read 'talky' where they read 'surface'), because a discriminator that outlives the node it names is a word that has to be read historically. `ctx.model_surface` is deliberately NOT renamed: it names the ROLE the model plays for the level, a cogny has a brain too, and the key is a public contract surface of its own. The level's own address space is what moved -- an override_params path or a mutation that named <assistant>/surface/... names <assistant>/talky/... from here on -- which is the second digit (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4). Since 2.4.0 both surfaces carry the credential lane's connect point (`talky@4.6.1`, `cogny@4.6.1`, GH #560): the member level may draw a v-lane from a brain in here straight to the person's own `access`, so a generation's models can run on a grant instead of on a key in their config. The generation itself declares nothing about that lane and takes no influence on it -- it is transparent, which is exactly what lets the v-lane skip it (GH #559, docs/development-rules.md § 8b). A caller can dock something here it could not dock before, so it is the second digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a). Since 2.4.0 ([#561](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/561), under the v-lane ruling of [#559](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/559)) the level no longer CARRIES the identity pack -- it vouches for it. `in_pack` and `pack_ack` keep their declarations and gain a connect point, `"at": ["./talky", "./cogny"]`, and the four pass-through edges are gone: thirty-seven edges become thirty-three. A level that declares a lane has said it takes part in it, and this one stamped nothing, filtered nothing and guarded nothing on the pack -- so the sender draws one v-lane per rim straight from the member's own `./affinity` and one back, and the two hops in between disappear. It is the second digit because an ADDRESS moved: a caller that wired `in_pack` at this level's own path redraws the edge at the two rims the corridor names. The lane set, the slots, the fan-out and the two receipts per pack are unchanged, and the pairing that obliges the receipt is now read at the rim, where talky and cogny declare it themselves. Since 2.4.1 both occupant pins move to `talky@4.6.1` / `cogny@4.6.1` (GH #570): a capped round of either occupant now ends on a named partial answer with `hop.partial` beside `hop.round_capped`, so the advice this level routes from the core to the surface is a sentence about the round rather than the raw tool payload the surface used to write into the conversation. Only the pins move -- no lane, no edge, no declaration of this level.
description.use_when: One per generation. Instantiate it into a member's `assistants` container and wire its transit lanes in the same mutation; the hive is an island until an edge crosses into it. NOTHING comes afterwards -- the level is complete at birth and there is no per-channel follow-up mutation any more. Give it its model and its prompt with `override_params` on `<assistant>/talky/brain` and `<assistant>/talky/collector`. The mutation that instantiates it also draws the one edge that makes it addressable: `./assistants -> ./assistants/<name>` on `in_turn`, guarded on `context.assistant == '<name>'` -- and, since GH #475, the same guard on `in_export` and `in_import`, because a member with two generations has two session ledgers and they are not one document. A generation swap replaces this node and the older one stays in place, silent and readable -- which is why the memory, the identity, the screen and now the channels are NOT here: they belong to the member, and a swap must not reset what the person is known to be or how they are reached.
description.not_in_scope: No channel and no connector: since 2.0.0 a channel is the MEMBER's (GH #454). A bot this level owned would be a bot one agent owned, and a person's second agent could not be reached through it; a shared screen would have no owner at all. No memory hive, no identity store and no memory-drain: the memory belongs to the MEMBER (GH #122, ADR 0012), and per-turn extraction (GH #298, ruling Q11) replaced the drain -- `extraction` leaves this level on a lane of its own. No firewall: the screen sits outside the generation so that two channels of one person meet ONE view of an attacker and the rate window does not restart because a generation was replaced (GH #302). No terminal and no sink of any kind (ruling Q2, GH #284): `error` leaves the level and becomes no_route in the DLQ if nobody consumes it, which is recorded and self-localising. No tool schemas and no per-tool credentials -- a schema lives in the calling brain's `system.tools` and a credential in the cell that needs it. No second surface: two session stores of one generation would have to be told apart before a sweep could run.
examples: PORTS - the assistant is an OPEN hive: it declares no params.ports, because it is a level that gets wired INTO and sealing it would refuse exactly the endpoints the member's own container needs. Entry lanes, all eight addressed at the assistant path itself: 'in_turn' (the screened turn coming back from the member's firewall, carrying context.channel, context.user_id, context.audience_set and context.assistant), 'in_advice' (a second agent's answer, arriving as its own turn), 'in_sweep', 'in_prune', 'in_round_sweep' (operator housekeeping), 'in_build_result' (the builder's answer) and, since GH #475, 'in_export' and 'in_import' (the transfer lanes of this generation's session keeper, pure transit). Exits, all eight leaving the assistant path: 'answer' (what this generation said, on its way back to the channel that asked), 'write', 'turn_write', 'extraction' (to the member's memory hive in_remember door), 'prune', 'error', 'build' and 'dump' (the parts and receipts of a transfer, drained with a PLAIN hop.route == 'dump' edge into the member's own export sink). Five pairings are declared in params.required_drains: in_turn -> error, in_prune -> prune, in_pack -> pack_ack, in_export -> dump and in_import -> dump. FOUR more lanes are declared and are NOT at the assistant path: since 2.4.0 'in_pack'/'pack_ack' (GH #561) and 'recall'/'in_bundle' (GH #562) carry at: ["./talky", "./cogny"] and are V-LANES (ADR-0020) -- the identity pack and the memory road both end on the two occupants themselves, one hop from the member's assistants container, and this level's part in either is the PERMISSION rather than a pass-through. The eight edges that used to make those hops are gone; what draws the new ones is the mutation that instantiates the generation, one per occupant per direction, each naming its lane. A level in between that declares the lane and names no connect point may not be skipped (v_lane_mandatory_hop), which is how the member's stamping door stays in every recall road. And an edge that still delivers one of the four AT this path is refused (hive_contract): a connect point closes the rim for its lane.

WHAT 2.0.0 CHANGED, exactly: `channels` -- an open container -- became ONE ref on talky@4.3.0 (called `surface` until 2.3.0, `talky` since); the emit `turn` was REMOVED and the emit `answer` was added. Both fall out of the level rule rather than out of a decision. The raw wire that produced `turn` now sits in the member's channels container and reaches the member's screen without crossing this level; the `answer` that a connector used to consume INSIDE this level has no consumer here any more, so it crosses. Taking a lane and an address away is the first digit -- neither rule of docs/development-rules.md § 4 covers a removal.

the tool exit is ONE edge and it names no tool: ./talky -> ./tools is a single GUARDED DEFAULT on hop.route == 'tool'. The ONE consult errand (consult_cogny -- `ask_memory` was retired in GH #530) is an ordinary conditioned edge on hop.tool_name, so a consult fires a regular edge and the default stays silent, while a real tool call fires nothing regular and the default carries it. The exclusion chain that used to name every tool is gone entirely.

WHERE THE SIXTEEN LANES COME FROM: the union of what this level's three occupants accept and emit at the versions pinned in each `because` (talky in ./talky, cogny, tools), minus the lanes a sibling inside the level consumes itself -- tool, tool_call/tool_result and in_tool -- and minus the FOUR that are declared but do not stand at this path: since 2.4.0 `in_pack`/`pack_ack` (GH #561) and `recall`/`in_bundle` (GH #562) name connect points (`at`) and dock on the two occupants as v-lanes, so they are the level's declaration without being its rim (ADR-0020). `answer` used to be a fourth subtraction and is one no longer, which is the whole of GH #454 read off the derivation rule. GH #475 is the rule read in the other direction: nothing inside this level consumes in_export, in_import or dump, so all three cross and are declared. If an occupant moves a lane, this level moves with it in the same commit: crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh302_assistant_wires_channels_once.rs reads those files and fails until it does.

adding a second channel costs NOTHING here. It is one add_nodes into <member>/channels and two edges of the member's, and this level does not learn about it: a turn from any channel arrives on the same in_turn door and the answer leaves on the same answer lane, with context.channel telling the member where to send it back. Adding a second ASSISTANT costs one edge per direction in the member's container -- see templates/member/README.md, 'Addressing an assistant through a channel'.

model_surface.because: the model the CONVERSATION SURFACE infers with -- a talky-class model, and deliberately not ctx.model, which reaches the reasoning core. One flat ctx serves both occupants of this level, so without a key of its own the surface runs the core's model and the whole point of the split is gone (GH #516). A RESOLVED literal or a MODEL_<ROLE> env token passed verbatim, same two forms as ctx.model.
